instruction: Vision signal: 62% fall armyworm, 31% stem borer. Farmer: Oghere dị n'akwụkwọ ọka m. Kedu pest bụ nke a?
response: Signal ahụ adịghị ike iji kpọọ pest ahụ n'aka. Oghere ndị ahụ dị n'olulu ọka? Ị na-ahụ frass ọhụrụ n'ebe ahụ? Ị nwere ike ịkọwa larva ma ọ bụrụ na ị hụrụ ya? Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Vision signal: 62% fall armyworm, 31% stem borer. Farmer: There are holes in my maize leaves. What is it?
response: The signal is not strong enough to name the pest confidently. Are the holes concentrated in the maize whorl, and do you see fresh frass there? Also, can you see a caterpillar with a pale upside-down Y on its head? Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Manomi: Na ga ramuka marasa daidaito da sabon bayan gari a ramin masara.\nMataimaki: Wannan na iya zama kwaron soja.\nManomi: Ban ga tsutsar ba. Me zan yi?
response: Har yanzu za ka iya bincike ba tare da ganin tsutsar ba. Duba shuke-shuke da dama don sabon cizo da sabon bayan gari, sannan ka rubuta shuke-shuken da ke fama a yanzu. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Kedu ka m ga-esi amata fall armyworm site na caterpillar ọzọ?
response: Chọọ akara Y gbagoro n'isi caterpillar na ntụpọ ojii anọ dị ka square n'akụkụ ahụ nke dị nso n'isi ọdụ. Frass dị n'ime olulu ọka bụkwa ihe ngosi dị mkpa. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Ta yaya zan bambanta kwaron soja da wata tsutsa?
response: Ka nemi alamar Y mai juyewa a gaban kan tsutsar da kuma ɗigo huɗu masu duhu da suka yi kama da murabba'i a sashen jikin kusa da ƙarshe. Bayan gari a cikin ramin masara ma alama ce mai amfani. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: How I fit know say na fall armyworm, no be another caterpillar?
response: Look for the pale upside-down Y mark for the front of the dark head and four dark spots arranged like a square near the last body segment. Fresh frass for the maize whorl na another useful sign. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Can I identify FAW just by the damage?
response: Damage alone is not enough for a confident identification. Ragged holes and fresh frass in the whorl are strong clues, but inspect the caterpillar for the characteristic head and body markings. Source: FAO Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Farmer: Ahụrụ m oghere na frass ọhụrụ n'olulu ọka.\nAssistant: Nke a nwere ike ịbụ fall armyworm.\nFarmer: Ahụghị m caterpillar. Kedu ihe m ga-eme?
response: Ị ka nwere ike ịme scouting n'enweghị ịhụ larva. Lelee ọtụtụ osisi maka mmebi ọhụrụ na frass ọhụrụ, ma gụọ naanị osisi ndị nwere infestation ugbu a. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Àwọn àmì wo ni ó wà nínú ihò àgbàdo tí ń fi hàn pé ọ̀gbìn ológun àgbàdo wà?
response: Àwọn ihò ìjẹ tuntun àti ìgbẹ́ tuntun (frass) nínú ihò àgbàdo ń fi hàn pé ìdin ń jẹ ọ̀gbìn lọ́wọ́. Ṣàyẹ̀wò ihò, kì í ṣe àwọn ihò àtijọ́ nìkan. Source: FAO, FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Wadanne alamu a cikin ramin masara ke nuna kwaron soja (fall armyworm)?
response: Sabbin ramukan cizo da sabon bayan gari (frass) a cikin ramin masara na nuna cewa tsutsa tana cin abinci a yanzu. Ka duba ramin, ba tsoffin ramuka kawai ba. Source: FAO, FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Ìfihàn àwòrán: 62% ọ̀gbìn ológun, 31% stem borer. Àgbẹ̀: Ihò wà lórí ewé àgbàdo. Kí ni?
response: Ìdámọ̀ náà kò lágbára tó láti dájú. Ṣé àwọn ihò wà nínú ihò àgbàdo, àti pé ṣé frass tuntun wà níbẹ̀? Ṣe o lè ṣàpèjúwe ìdin tí o bá rí? Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Kedu ihe na-egosi fall armyworm n'ime olulu ọka?
response: Oghere ọhụrụ na akwụkwọ na nsị ọhụrụ (frass) n'ime olulu ọka na-egosi na larva na-eri nri ugbu a. Lelee olulu, ọ bụghị naanị oghere ochie. Source: FAO, FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Which signs for maize dey show say fall armyworm dey?
response: Fresh ragged holes and fresh frass inside the maize whorl fit show say FAW larva dey feed now. Check the whorl, no be old holes only. Source: FAO, FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Farmer: I see ragged holes and fresh frass for the maize whorl.\nAssistant: That fit be fall armyworm.\nFarmer: I no see the caterpillar. Wetin now?
response: You can still scout without finding the larva. Check several plants for fresh whorl damage and fresh frass, then record only plants with current signs. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Àgbẹ̀: Mo rí ihò àti frass tuntun nínú ihò àgbàdo.\nOlùrànlọ́wọ́: Èyí lè jẹ́ ọ̀gbìn ológun.\nÀgbẹ̀: Mi ò rí ìdin. Kí ni mo ṣe?
response: O tún lè ṣe ìwòran láìrí ìdin náà. Ṣàyẹ̀wò ọ̀pọ̀ ewéko fún ìbàjẹ́ tuntun àti frass tuntun, kí o sì ka àwọn tó ní ìjàkadi lọ́wọ́ nìkan. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Farmer: I found ragged holes in the whorl and fresh frass.\nAssistant: That can indicate fall armyworm. Check the larva for an upside-down Y on the head.\nFarmer: I cannot see the larva. What now?
response: You can still scout for FAW without finding the larva. Check several plants for recent whorl damage and fresh frass, and record only plants showing current signs. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: How can I tell fall armyworm from another caterpillar?
response: Look for a pale upside-down Y on the front of the dark head and four dark spots forming a square on the second-to-last abdominal segment. Frass in the maize whorl is another useful clue. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Báwo ni mo ṣe lè mọ ọ̀gbìn ológun àgbàdo yàtọ̀ sí ìdin míì?
response: Wá àmì Y tí ó yí padà lórí iwájú orí ìdin àti àmì mẹ́rin dúdú tí wọ́n ṣe àgbékalẹ̀ onígun mẹ́rin lórí apá ara tó sún mọ́ ìkẹyìn. Frass nínú ihò àgbàdo tún jẹ́ àmì tó wúlò. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Vision signal: 62% fall armyworm, 31% stem borer. Farmer: Holes dey my maize leaves. Which pest be this?
response: The signal no strong enough to confirm. The holes dey mainly inside the maize whorl? You see fresh frass there? Can you describe the caterpillar if you find am? Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Alamar hoton gona: 62% kwaron soja, 31% stem borer. Manomi: Ramuka ne a ganyen masara. Menene?
response: Alamar ba ta da ƙarfi don in tabbatar. Shin ramukan suna tattare a cikin ramin masara, kuma akwai sabon bayan gari a wurin? Za ka iya bayyana yadda tsutsar take idan ka same ta? Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.
